messages.legacy.no_internal: No internal values available yet. Configure MQTT sources first.
messages.heating.central.intro: The boiler is switched on as soon as at least one room requests heat. It is switched off only once no request remains and the burner is detected as off. Whether a room receives its heat from here or from its local device is decided by the outdoor temperature against the limit temperature set per room. The system-wide outdoor temperature from Settings → MQTT is used; the field below overrides it for the heating only.
messages.heating.central.burner_feedback_hint: Flame signal or “burner on” contact. Determines the times used for heating cost; without it the rising flow temperature is used instead
messages.heating.central.outdoor_hint: Empty = system-wide outdoor temperature from the MQTT settings
messages.heating.central.flow_return_hint: With a switch actuator both temperatures are monitored mandatorily. Without burner feedback, homeESS detects from the flow temperature whether it is running: several consecutive readings rising mean “burner on” (a single fluctuation is not enough), the holding phase that follows still counts towards it, and only several consecutive readings falling end the firing phase. As long as the burner is firing, the boiler stays switched on. The return lags a full circuit behind — it is displayed and logged, but decides nothing.
messages.heating.central.return_hint: Is monitored and displayed; switching off is decided by the flow temperature
messages.heating.central.min_delta_hint: Smaller differences count as noise and are ignored for burner detection
messages.heating.central.wait_hint: Only relevant if neither feedback nor flow temperature is available
messages.heating.central.max_hold_hint: 0 = none: the boiler stays on as long as the burner is detected as firing
messages.heating.central.pump_hint: Optional second switching target for the switch actuator. If it is set, the following is mandatory: first the pump runs, then the burner starts — and after the burner is switched off the pump keeps running for the configured time before it too switches off. If the state reports the pump status back, the burner additionally waits for that feedback.
messages.heating.central.consumption_hint: Consumption and heating cost are calculated from the logged burner runtime using these figures.
messages.heating.central.title: Central heating
messages.heating.not_configured: Not configured — rooms so far control only their own devices.
messages.heating.add_room_hint: The name determines the room's states (System / Rooms / <name>). Temperature sources, devices, contacts and the central heating permission are then configured on the room's own page.
messages.heating.heat_offset_hint: Heating on at target minus offset
messages.heating.heat_offset_hint_long: Heating on at target minus offset — 0 means: exactly at the target temperature
messages.heating.cool_offset_hint: Cooling on at target plus offset
messages.heating.cool_min_hint: Below this it never cools — empty = no lower limit
messages.heating.cool_min_hint_long: Below this it never cools — a night setback on the thermostat therefore does not wake the air conditioner. Empty = no lower limit. If target plus offset is higher, that value applies.
messages.heating.hysteresis_hint: Prevents constant switching on and off
messages.heating.hysteresis_hint_long: Gap between the switch-on and switch-off point so the system does not cycle
messages.heating.remove_room_hint: The room, its temperature sources, its contacts and its states are permanently deleted.
messages.heating.billing.since_start: since the start of the period
messages.heating.billing.start_value_hint: What was already consumed since the last meter reading, before homeESS started counting. It only shifts the total; the running period remains.
messages.heating.billing.close_hint: The running period is stored as the previous one and the new one starts at 0. This cannot be undone.
messages.heating.billing.metered_hint: The actual consumption of the period according to the meter
messages.heating.billing.calibrate_hint: Use this to calibrate the estimated consumption per operating hour
messages.heating.billing.calibrate_note: Calibration adjusts the consumption per operating hour to the value read off. This only makes sense if no other consumers are connected to the same meter and the starting value is correct.
messages.heating.room.name_hint: Appears in the room's state topics — renaming changes them
messages.heating.room.thermostat_hint: The target temperature stays synchronised in both directions, e.g. Homematic IP wall thermostat
messages.heating.room.central_allowed: This room may request the central heating
messages.heating.room.central_temp: Central heating from outdoor temperature below (°C)
messages.heating.room.fan_hint: Is switched on while this room requests heat from the central heating, and off again afterwards
messages.heating.room.no_cool_device: No cooling device has been configured for this room yet — the setting takes effect as soon as the “cooling on” sequence contains actions.
messages.heating.room.reset_time_hint: Empty = only when the target temperature is reached
messages.heating.room.contacts_hint: If an assigned contact is open, heating and cooling are switched off. With a delay, brief airing has no effect; 0 seconds switches off immediately. Closing always takes effect immediately.
messages.heating.room.add_sensor_hint: Several sources per room are possible — their average then counts as the actual temperature.
messages.heating.room.add_contact_hint: Window and door contacts block heating and cooling while they are open.
messages.heating.room.page_title: Room in the heating & climate module
messages.heating.room.priority_hint: The priority is the operating level from which a device is allowed to run (1 = highest, always runs; 5 = only with free surplus). If the current operating level does not cover the priority, the device stays off and is switched off immediately when the level drops.
messages.heating.room.central_fallback: If the operating level blocks the heating device, the central heating may step in
messages.heating.room.central_fallback_hint: If this is enabled, the outdoor temperature limit no longer applies to this room in the meantime: instead of the blocked local device, the central heating heats directly. As soon as the operating level covers the priority again, the limit applies once more. This requires that the room is allowed to request the central heating.
messages.heating.room.sequences_hint: The heating and cooling devices are switched via action sequences — value assignments, pauses and loops that can check cyclically whether the desired state was actually reached. This also allows operating a split air conditioner that needs operating mode, target temperature and switch-on command one after another. Both devices are optional: a room without actions in the “on” sequence only records its temperature.
messages.weather.title: Weather
messages.weather.all_days_hint: Temperature and solar intensity as lines, precipitation per hour as bars.
messages.weather.more_days_hint: Brief overview of the days after the detailed period.
messages.weather.pv_forecast_yield: Expected yield according to the PV forecast
messages.grid.title: Grid control
messages.grid.verify_hint: Switching commands are verified against the broker feedback and repeated automatically if they differ.
messages.grid.blackout_delay: Wait time until backup power detection (seconds)
messages.grid.soc_hint: Lower and upper are separate switching windows. In the range between them this output stays off.
messages.grid.hysteresis_hint: At most 5 %, effective only directly at the respective limit.
messages.grid.temp_warning_hint: Unless specified otherwise, the value 1 or true is recognised as a warning.
messages.grid.inverter_load_hint: Readings come directly from Power consumption → Self-consumption power L1–L3. The grid switching uses its own on/off thresholds. The stepwise load shedding works separately with 80 % of the configured maximum load per phase and only releases again in steps below 50 %.
messages.grid.off_delay_hint: 0 switches off without delay. A running delay is retained across a homeESS restart.
messages.pool.sensor_hint: Sensor topics for water temperature and water quality.
messages.pool.solar_hint: Switches automatically in direct sunlight. After each switch the state is held for at least 2 minutes. When the maximum temperature is reached, the pump changes to a sampling mode (30 s every 30 min).
messages.pool.filter_hint: Fixed filter times or coupling to the solar pump control. The battery override switches the pump on additionally as soon as a configurable state of charge is reached.
messages.pool.grid_disabled_hint: Grid control is disabled. The load shedding phase is only used when the module is active.
messages.pool.follow_solar: Pump follows the solar pump control (filter times are ignored)
messages.cinema.change_hint: Every change of state calls the room's “on” or “off” action sequence.
messages.cinema.state_hint: Every room gets a writable cinema mode state under “System / Home cinema”, named after it.
messages.cinema.sync_hint: Is kept synchronised with the cinema mode in both directions
messages.cinema.delete_hint: The room, its cinema mode state and both action sequences are permanently deleted.
messages.cinema.title: Home cinema
messages.cinema.actions_on_off: Actions of the on / off sequence
messages.cinema.sequence_off_hint: Runs as soon as the cinema mode is switched off.
messages.forecast.selfcount_hint_empty: Self-counting vs. balance per hour. Collects values from the next measuring interval onwards.
messages.forecast.selfcount_hint: Self-counting (self-consumption power) vs. meter/balance based source per hour. The current hour grows until the end of the hour; the marker shows the value adopted into the forecast.
messages.forecast.heating_curve_hint: Measured average power of the heating / climate function group per 1 °C window of the outdoor temperature (average of up to the last 30 measuring days; the marker line shows today's value). From this the forecast calculates the expected consumption per hour according to the predicted outdoor temperature.
messages.forecast.no_power_curve: No power curve yet: currently no outdoor temperature is coming in (check the topic in the settings, or the sensor/server) and no measurement data is available yet. As soon as measuring days feed into the temperature windows — a power of 0 W is a valid measurement here — the curve appears.
messages.forecast.outdoor_axis_hint: Outdoor temperature (°C) · bar height = average power (W) across all 24 hours · marker = today's value · click a bar for the 24-hour curve
messages.forecast.soc_next_charge: SoC at the next charging start
messages.forecast.overview_hint: PV yield, dynamic consumption and battery trend for today plus three days.
messages.forecast.model_hint: The annual average stabilises the start. With every complete day the moving average gains more weight; the hourly profile learns when energy is typically needed in the house.
messages.forecast.battery_params_hint: Battery capacity, minimum SoC and efficiencies are maintained on the battery page.
messages.forecast.max_deviation_hint: If the balance of a completed hour deviates more than this, self-counting takes over.
messages.forecast.min_deviation_hint: Below this absolute deviation the guard never applies (noise protection for small hours).
messages.forecast.autarky_mqtt_hint: Optional bidirectional synchronisation of the annual counters.
messages.forecast.hour_axis_hint: Hour of day (0–23) · bar height = average power (W) · marker = today's value
messages.forecast.not_expected_in_range: not expected within the visible forecast period
messages.battery.topics_hint: Values are obtained via the configured MQTT broker. Leave empty to hide a display.
messages.battery.topic_min_soc: Minimum state of charge – target topic (%)
messages.battery.topic_min_soc_remote: Minimum state of charge – remote topic (bidirectional synchronisation)
messages.battery.min_soc_remote_hint: Changes to the minimum state of charge are mirrored here; if this topic changes externally, the minimum state of charge follows.
messages.battery.min_soc_steps_hint: Is stored in steps of 5 % and sent to the configured target topic.
messages.battery.type_hint: The battery type sets suggestions per cell. The lower and upper total voltage can be adjusted manually at any time.
messages.wallbox.overview_hint: Master data, MQTT topics and charging mode priorities in one view.
messages.wallbox.topics_hint: Only the control topic is required. The control topic is a pure actuator (homeESS switches the wallbox through it). The optional control sync topic mirrors the on/off state in both directions: homeESS writes to it when switching itself; an external change (on the remote device) counts as an operating command (ON → charge to full, OFF during charging → off until the next day). Without a status topic, the sync or control topic serves as the actual state.
messages.wallbox.mode_sync_hint: The mode sync topic only keeps the charging plan synchronised in both directions: 1 = private, 2 = work, 3 = always full. It does not switch charging on or off.
messages.wallbox.priority_hint: Priority = operating level from which charging is allowed (1 = always, 5 = only with surplus).
messages.wallbox.workdays: Work: working days (the car is ready with the minimum charge level for work)
messages.wallbox.workdays_hint: For a working day the car is charged in time up to the minimum charge level for work; above that only PV surplus as in private mode. If the charge level falls below it on a working day, it is topped up immediately.
messages.wallbox.private_rule_from: Private rule from (time) before a free following day
messages.wallbox.restart_hint: If, despite a charging command, the charging process remains below the idle threshold after the specified time, it is switched off and on again once for one minute (restart). Only effective with a power topic.
messages.wallbox.intro: Every wallbox is controlled and measured via MQTT. The charging mode (private / work / always full) regulates predictively against PV surplus and the minimum SoC of the house battery.
messages.measure.topic_required: At least one topic for switching, power or meter is required.
messages.measure.topics_hint: Without a status topic, the switching topic counts as the actual state. If only a meter is set, the power is derived from the meter progress (0 W after more than 10 min without progress). Without a power and meter topic, power and energy are instead calculated virtually from rated power × switching state — without a rated power there is no measurement.
messages.measure.remote_sync_hint: Is kept synchronised with the switching state in both directions.
messages.measure.level_hint: All devices are switched off as soon as the operating level falls below their priority. Always on: when released again the device switches back on automatically; otherwise it stays off until switched on manually. Priority = operating level from which the device is allowed to run (1 = always, 5 = only with surplus).
messages.measure.load_shed_hint: With grid control active, the device can be shed before the grid is connected: from 80 % of the configured inverter load on the selected phase, or on any of the three phases with three-phase power. Always on switches back on automatically below 50 % of the corresponding load threshold.
messages.measure.three_phase_hint: Three-phase treats the device as evenly distributed across L1, L2 and L3.
messages.measure.grid_disabled: Grid control is disabled. These settings are only available once the module is activated.
messages.measure.inherit_function: (devices without their own function inherit it)
messages.measure.offset_total: Offset the consumption total against the total consumption
messages.measure.meter_group: Meter group (its own devices are meters; the total consumption is fixed, subgroups are deducted as “other consumers”)
messages.measure.meter_group_hint: An offset meter group is a barrier layer: if its “offset against total consumption” box is ticked, it contributes the full branch value to the house consumption; the subgroups are then no longer offset globally in addition. The box of a subgroup instead controls whether its consumption is offset against the next higher meter group — that is, deducted from its “other consumers” — or remains included in it.
messages.measure.switch_hint: Switch on/off (switching on only with a released priority)
messages.measure.mode_title: Operating mode or active priority to which this device responds at the operating level
messages.measure.group_minus_sub: Total power of the meter group minus the total power of the subgroups
messages.measure.meter_group_short: Meter group: its own devices are meters; the total consumption is fixed.
messages.measure.move_group_hint: Move group: drag onto another group (subgroup) or onto free space (top level)
messages.measure.always_on_level: Always on (automatically via the operating level)
messages.dashboard.chart_failed: The chart could not be loaded.
messages.dashboard.no_switch_targets: No switchable targets available. Create a device with a switching topic or a switch group under Measure + switch — or a room in the home cinema module.
messages.dashboard.tab_follows_group: The tab follows the selected group.
messages.dashboard.optional_state_name: (optional, otherwise the name of the state)
messages.dashboard.series_hint: Colour and name per line can be chosen freely; without a name the data series appears in the legend. All lines of a tile share one value axis — they should therefore use the same unit.
messages.dashboard.gaps_hint: What happens when there are no values in the database for a period — for instance because the server was off. “Leave gap” shows the outage; the other settings add points that were not actually measured.
messages.dashboard.weather_choice_hint: “Current weather” shows the situation right now, a day shows the forecast. The selection is relative — “tomorrow” stays tomorrow, even the day after.
messages.dashboard.shown_values_hint: Without a tick the tile shows a sensible default selection. The header with the weather situation and the key value is always shown.
messages.dashboard.move_contents_to: Move the contained groups and widgets to
messages.dashboard.save_failed: Saving failed. The changes have not been applied yet — please try again.
messages.dashboard.no_series_db: The database does not contain any data series yet. The InfluxDB adapter fills it as soon as history is enabled for a state.
messages.dashboard.db_unreachable: The database is unreachable. Check Settings → General → Database.
messages.dashboard.fill_hint: Fill the area between the line and the zero line in the line colour
messages.dashboard.opacity: Opacity of the area in percent
messages.dashboard.order_save_failed: The arrangement could not be saved — it will be retried when applying.
messages.dashboard.switch_blocked: Switching on is currently blocked (priority/operating level).
messages.conditions.intro: A condition consists of a trigger and a then branch; if and else can be enabled with a tick. A loop needs none of these: its cyclic check is at the same time the execution condition.
messages.conditions.loop_check_hint: The check is mandatory here: it is evaluated at the specified interval, and as long as it does not apply the loop runs again. Further actions are then added via the loop's plus sign.
messages.conditions.op_gte: is greater than or equal to
messages.conditions.op_lte: is less than or equal to
messages.conditions.branch_hint: Triggers start the evaluation, all if clauses are checked together, and then the then branch runs — or the else branch. Then and else are action sequences: they run from top to bottom and may contain pauses and loops.
messages.conditions.check_cyclic_hint: The condition is checked again and again at the specified interval — counted from the last run of this loop, or from the start of homeESS. If it does not apply, only this loop is run again. Only the branch that was executed last is checked.
messages.conditions.delete_hint: The element is permanently removed from the condition. With a loop, all of its contents disappear as well.
messages.conditions.triggered_by_check: Triggered by the cyclic check of its loop
messages.conditions.layout_save_failed: The layout could not be saved.
messages.conditions.order_save_failed: The order could not be saved.
messages.sequences.intro: The actions of a sequence run from top to bottom. Loops repeat their contents and can additionally check cyclically whether the desired state was actually reached.
messages.sequences.check_hint: The condition is checked again and again at the specified interval — counted from the last run of this loop, or from the start of homeESS. If it does not apply, only this loop is run again. Only the sequence belonging to the current state is checked.
messages.sequences.remove_hint: The action is permanently removed. With a loop, all of its contents disappear as well.
messages.pv.overview_hint: Master data, installation parameters and MQTT assignment in one compact view.
messages.pv.efficiency_hint: Module/system efficiency for calibrating the ideal value (at 20 °C). When a cell type is selected it is pre-filled with a typical default for that type — freely fine-tunable. The device efficiency of the converter is taken into account separately.
messages.pv.device_efficiency_hint: Device efficiency (MPPT controller, inverter, …), temperature-dependent at outdoor temperature level.
messages.pv.before_noon_hint: Before solar noon: the system only counts as a sun reference if its clear-sky ideal value reaches at least this share of its kWp peak power — otherwise it distorts the ratio when the sun is low or to the side. Default 10 %.
messages.pv.yield_counter_hint: Cumulative meter reading (raw value). Only the increments are counted as the daily yield.
messages.pv.day_start_hint: Enter the value at the start of the day. The current daily yield is then added and carried forward automatically.
messages.pv.year_start_hint: Enter the starting value and date of a day in the current year. Minimum, maximum, average and date are derived from it automatically.
messages.consumption.self_counter_hint: If these three meters are set and deliver values, their daily increment (plus PV fed in on the consumer side) counts as the actual self-consumption — instead of the balance of PV, grid and battery.
messages.consumption.day_start_hint: Enter grid import and feed-in at the start of the day. Self-consumption is calculated from PV yield plus grid import minus feed-in.
messages.settings.appearance_hint: The colour theme applies only to the signed-in user and colours the working area of the pages only. The title bar and side menu keep their colours in every theme.
messages.settings.database_hint: Central time-series database for charts and evaluations (InfluxDB 1.x). This can be the database the InfluxDB adapter writes to, or any other — including one on a different server. On the settings page of an InfluxDB adapter instance, the button “Adopt as the default database for homeESS” is enough to copy those details here.
messages.settings.db_disabled_hint: Without a tick, charts do not query any data.
messages.settings.tls_hint: Only with https. Switch off if the server uses a self-signed certificate.
messages.settings.update_hint: Checks stable releases from the official GitHub repository. The check runs independently; automatic installation is separate from it, switched off by default and takes place exclusively within the defined maintenance window.
messages.settings.check_interval_hint: This interval applies regardless of automatic installation. As soon as a newer version is available, the notice appears in the header. After a failed check the next attempt is brought forward.
messages.settings.auto_install: Install found versions automatically within the maintenance window
messages.settings.window_hint: The maintenance window defines only when an update that has already been found may be installed. It uses the homeESS time zone configured above; identical start and end times mean all day, and a window spanning midnight is possible.
messages.settings.theme_hint: Colours only the working area of the pages; the title bar and menu stay the same.
messages.settings.theme_dark: All pages on a dark background.
messages.settings.theme_dashboard_dark: Only the dashboard dark, all other pages light.
messages.customstates.name_hint: The name and position in the directory tree can be changed at any time.
messages.customstates.edit_hint: The definition, storage location and current value can be edited in full.
messages.customstates.delete_folder: The directory and all of its contents are deleted.
messages.customstates.delete_folder_hint: All contained subdirectories and states are permanently lost.
messages.customstates.delete_state: The custom state is permanently deleted.
messages.customstates.set_failed: The value could not be set.
messages.energy.title: Energy
messages.energy.intro: The most important figures of the energy pages at a glance. Each section leads to the detailed page with configuration and history.
messages.energy.consumption_hint: Self-consumption and grid import over time.
messages.energy.battery_hint: State of charge, power and reserve of the storage system.
messages.energy.grid_hint: Switching states of the grid and feed-in control.
messages.switch.remote_hint: Is kept synchronised with the group's switching state in both directions.
messages.switch.timer_hint: When the time elapses, the entire group is switched off.
messages.switch.as_unit_hint: As a unit: if one device is switched on or off, the others are brought to the same state. Without this option the group counts as on as soon as at least one device is on.
messages.switch.none_yet: No switch group created yet. Create the first group via “Add switch group”.
messages.switch.drag_to_assign: Drag into a switch group to assign
messages.switch.as_unit_title: The group switches as a unit: every on/off edge brings the others along.
messages.switch.state_title: Switching state of the group (on as soon as one device is on)
messages.switch.switch_title: Switch the group: switching on turns all devices on, switching off turns all off.
messages.energyflow.intro: Live flow from the sources (PV, grid, battery) via self-consumption to the consumption groups. Subgroups and the “other” remainder branch further to the right; individual devices are deliberately not shown. A colour can be chosen per group via the pencil icon.
messages.energyflow.no_values: No values available yet. As soon as PV, grid, battery or group data is available, the energy flow appears here.
messages.energyflow.export_hint: Publicly accessible live views of the diagram. The URL is derived from the name; the theme determines the light or dark appearance.
messages.states.format_hint: Empty decimal places leave the value unchanged. The unit is appended to the value in the display and overrides the source's unit.
messages.states.instance_stopped: This instance is not running at the moment. Changes will be applied at the next start.
messages.states.already_used: This state is already used here.

messages.heating.room.central_hint: The decisive factor is the outdoor temperature: if it is below the given limit, the central heating supplies the room instead of the local heating device; the same switching hysteresis applies. Above it, only the local device heats — if none is configured, no heating takes place in this range by design. Whether the room needs heat at all is still decided by its own temperature against the target temperature.
messages.heating.room.central_not_configured: The central heating is not configured at the moment.
messages.heating.room.climate_override_hint: This room's air conditioner can be overridden by hand via the state {topic} (0 = off, 1 = on, 2 = automatic). A manual switch suspends the automatic action loops — the unit then responds neither to an open contact nor to the room temperature. It returns to automatic as soon as the room reaches the target temperature — and, if a time is set here, at that time at the latest. What counts is the first occurrence after switching: if you select “on” at 23:00, the return at 22:00 happens the following day.
